section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 Minute)
section_1.content: Briefly define a basis as a 'coordinate system'. Use a 2D grid overlay to show that any vector can be reached using basis vectors (i, j). Introduce the core question: 'How do we describe the same physical vector if we change our perspective (basis)?'
section_1.example: Visualize a treasure map where the 'grid' lines are rotated. Even if the grid changes, the 'X marks the spot' location in the world remains the same.

section_2.title: The Mechanism of Coordinate Transformation (1.5 Minutes)
section_2.content: Explain that a coordinate transformation is essentially mapping 'Old Coordinates' to 'New Coordinates' using a Change-of-Basis Matrix (P). Visualize P as columns of new basis vectors expressed in terms of the old basis.
section_2.example: Imagine a robot dog moving in a square room. If the dog's local 'forward' direction changes, we use matrix P to translate its 'local' steps into the 'global' room coordinates.

section_3.title: The Change-of-Basis Formula (1.5 Minutes)
section_3.content: Formulate the equation: [v]_B = P_inv * [v]_A. Use animation to show the multiplication of the matrix against the vector. Emphasize that P represents the transformation from New to Old, so its inverse is required to convert Old to New.
section_3.example: Use a camera analogy: The object is the vector. The 'Old Basis' is the world frame, and the 'New Basis' is the camera's lens frame. P allows the computer to calculate where pixels appear in the camera view.

section_4.title: Summary & Conceptual Application (1 Minute)
section_4.content: Conclude by emphasizing that the vector v is invariant—it doesn't change; only its description changes. Reiterate that this is the mathematical foundation for computer graphics (rotating objects) and data analysis (PCA).
section_4.example: Final visual: A 3D character rotating in a game engine. Show how 'Change of Basis' is what allows the game to calculate the character's limbs relative to their own body, rather than the static game world.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right side grid: x > 0
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 1.5 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & Intuition", [
            "A basis is like a coordinate system.",
            "Basis vectors define our grid.",
            "Any vector is a linear combination.",
            "Change perspectives, keep the vector.",
            "How do we describe this change?"
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A basis is like a coordinate system.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#87CEFA")
        dot = Dot(color="#87CEFA")
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Basis vectors define our grid.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        label = Text("Origin", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        label.next_to(dot, UP, buff=0.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Any vector is a linear combination.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#90EE90")
        square = Square(side_length=1.0, color="#90EE90")
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3')
        self.play(Transform(dot, square))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Change perspectives, keep the vector.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(square.animate.set_stroke(width=6))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
